result.topic_en: Euler finishes the subtraction of differences increasing by 231 from 10000 for the second case and finds no new square. He then treats the third case, 10000 − ½(7s−591)(33s−2758) = xx, by substituting s = 84 + t, tabulating the subtrahends, and subtracting their differences from 10021; no square occurs.
result.transcription:

A quadrato igitur 10000 ſubtrahantur differentiae numero 231 creſcentes
$\begin{array}{rcr} 10000 & \cdots & 10000 \\ \underline{214} & & \underline{17} \\ 9786 & \cdots & 9983 \\ \underline{445} & & \underline{248} \\ 9341 & \cdots & 9735 \\ \underline{676} & & \underline{479} \\ 8665 & \cdots & 9256 \\ \underline{907} & & \underline{710} \\ 7758 & \cdots & 8546 \\ \underline{1138} & & \underline{941} \\ 6620 & \cdots & 7605 \\ \underline{1369} & & \underline{1172} \\ 5251 & \cdots & 6433 \\ \underline{1600} & & \underline{1403} \\ 3651 & \cdots & 5030 \\ \underline{1831} & & \underline{1634} \\ 1820 & \cdots & 3396 \\ & & \underline{1865} \\ & & 1531 \end{array}$
Ubi iterum nullus numerus quadratus occurrit praeter 10000, qui autem dat caſum cognitum.

§. 69. Pro caſu tertio aequatio examinanda erit
$10000 - \frac{1}{2}(7s - 591)(33s - 2758) = xx$, quae igitur, poſito $s = 84 + t$, abibit in hanc:
$10000 - \frac{1}{2}(7t - 3)(33t + 14) = xx$. Prouti igitur $t$ valorem habet vel poſitivum vel negativum, numeri ſubtrahen-
